title: chunkization-latency-dollar-probe-mar2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory benchmark to understand the latency vs dollar tradeoffs when we split (chunkize) large requests into smaller decode chunks before sending to the runtime. This is a working note: rough numbers, short ASCII charts, open questions and next steps.

Background / motivation:
- Many clients send long single-turn prompts (e.g., chat history + system instructions) that produce long outputs.
- Hypothesis: chunking output into fixed-size decode windows (e.g., 64/128 tokens) + streaming can reduce p99 tail latency at modest cost increase; alternate hypothesis: chunking incurs overhead per-chunk RPC which inflates cost and p95.
- We want a quick scan across configurations to see where the sweet spot lies for typical product workloads (avg resp len 120–400 tokens).

What I ran (environment):
- Model: redwood-13b-v1 (fp16) hosted on t4-like GPU pool (lab cluster).
- Load fixture: synthetic chat requests sampled from production small-conversations anonymized (n=2k requests).
- Baseline: no chunkization (stream full decode).
- Chunk configs: chunk=64, chunk=128, chunk=256 tokens. Also an adaptive heuristic: chunk until remaining <=128 then final chunk.
- Batching: disabled for this probe (single-req scheduling) to isolate per-request RPC overhead.
- Observed metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec, estimated $/1k tokens (rough price model), CPU RPC overhead (ms), bytes on wire.

Raw summary (median of sample):
- avg request length: 210 tokens
- baseline tokens/sec: 530
- baseline p99: 920 ms
- baseline $/1k tokens (est): $0.85

ASCII table (config | p50 | p95 | p99 | tokens/sec | $/1k | note):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
baseline              | 120ms | 400ms | 920ms | 530 t/s | $0.85 | single decode, streaming
chunk-64              | 130ms | 520ms | 760ms | 480 t/s | $0.95 | more RPCs, p99 improved vs baseline
chunk-128             | 125ms | 460ms | 700ms | 510 t/s | $0.92 | good p99 improvement, low throughput loss
chunk-256             | 140ms | 480ms | 830ms | 495 t/s | $0.90 | fewer RPCs but longer per-chunk decode
adaptive-<=128        | 122ms | 430ms | 690ms | 505 t/s | $0.93 | best p99 overall for mixed lengths
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Quick interpretation:
- Counterintuitive finding: chunk-64 reduced p99 compared to baseline but increased p95 significantly; overhead of many small RPCs creates jitter at mid-percentiles.
- chunk-128 appears to be a practical sweet spot: p99 improves ~24% vs baseline while tokens/sec drops only ~4% and cost increases slightly (~8%).
- chunk-256 underperforms chunk-128 on p99 because larger chunks increase single-decode latency; reduces RPC count but not enough to beat chunk-128.
- Adaptive chunking matches chunk-128 on p99 while better across mixed-length requests.

ASCII latency distribution sketch (normalized counts, not exact):
Latency (ms) distribution, rough bars show relative mass at percentiles.
Baseline:       |#####---------|########------|###----------|#-----------|  p50  p90  p95  p99
chunk-64:       |#####---------|###########---|####---------|------------|
chunk-128:      |#####---------|#########-----|###----------|#-----------|
adaptive:       |#####---------|#########-----|###----------|#-----------|
Legend: left=lower latencies, right=tail. chunk-128 and adaptive shift mass left at tail.

Cost notes / back-of-envelope pricing:
- Pricing model used (lab estimate): base GPU time price + RPC egress & control-plane per-call amortized. For small-chunk strategy, we estimate an additional $0.05–0.12 per 1k tokens depending on request mix.
- For our sample: chunk-128 increases unit cost ~8% relative to baseline. chunk-64 ~12%.
- If customers are price-sensitive and prioritize average latency over p99, baseline remains attractive.

Performance breakdown (where time is spent):
- decode kernel time: ~65–80% of total per-chunk latency
- RPC handshake / scheduling: 12–20% per chunk (dominant for chunk-64)
- network serialization (gzipped): ~5–8%
- application-level stitching (client): ~<5%

Open observations / anomalies:
- A subset (~6%) of requests showed repeated 1xxms spikes with chunk-64 tied to RPC backpressure on the t4 pool during modest cluster load — need to re-run on dedicated node.
- Throughput degradation was non-linear when concurrent requests > 40: per-chunk overhead amplified contention for scheduling slots.
- CPU profiling shows an increased number of small allocations in the control plane path for chunk sizes < 128; possible optimization target.

Recommendations (practical):
1) Ship an optional chunk-128 preview knob in the streaming SDK with clear guidance: improves p99 for long outputs with ~8% cost delta. Label as "p99-first" mode.
2) Implement adaptive chunking (<=128 tail) server-side as an experiment: keep client API same, runtime decides chunk boundary to limit RPC count for short outputs.
3) Instrument detailed RPC latency histogram and control-plane CPU allocations for next run; re-benchmark on a dedicated dedicated-GPU pool and on Dedicated customers (reserved capacity) to compare.
4) Re-run tests with small batching enabled (batch size 2–4) to see if chunk-64 overhead can be amortized.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] File a perf issue for control-plane small-allocation path (assign Diego).
- [ ] Re-run this probe on dedicated nodes (Rina) and capture per-chunk scheduling latency.
- [ ] Draft a short console/marketing one-pager showing p99 improvement vs cost delta for "p99-first" mode.
- [ ] Add synthetic workload for very long outputs (>=1024 tokens) to see asymptotics.

Questions for the team:
- Is a ~8% increase in $/1k tokens acceptable for our "improve p99" story for hosted customers? (product/ pricing input required).
- For Dedicated customers with steady high throughput, would we enable chunk-128 by default, or leave as opt-in?

Links (relevant):
- Confluence sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/CHUNK+PROBE+2026
- Lab cluster runs (raw logs): s3://redwood-lab/chunk-probe/mar2026/
- Perf PR (control plane): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482

Appendix: brief method notes
- pXX computed from request wall time (client send -> final stitched output received).
- $/1k tokens computed from measured GPU wall time * lab GPU rate + additional per-RPC markup estimated from egress and controller calls. Absolute $ values are lab-proxy not production rates.
- Stability: 95% of test runs repeat within +/-5% for p95 and +/-10% for p99. chunk-64 p99 variance higher (~18%).

End working note. Feedback welcome — planning a more rigorous run if team agrees on chunk-128 direction.
